cases.sentence: Случилось так, что в это же время явился и Хоботов с ___.
cases.explain: «бромистым калием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: One day Mihail Averyanitch came after dinner when Andrey Yefimitch was lying on the sofa. It so happened that Hobotov arrived at the same time with his bromide. Andrey Yefimitch got up heavily and sat down, leaning both arms on the sofa.

cases.sentence: ___, бог даст, махнем на Кавказ и весь его верхом объедем – гоп! гоп! гоп!
cases.explain: «Будущим летом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “We’ll show what we can do,” laughed Mihail Averyanitch, and he slapped his friend on the knee. “We’ll show them yet! Next summer, please God, we shall be off to the Caucasus, and we will ride all over it on horseback—trot, trot, trot! And when we are back from the Caucasus I shouldn’t wonder if we will all dance at the wedding.” Mihail Averyanitch gave a sly wink. “We’ll marry you, my dear boy, we’ll marry you. …”

cases.sentence: – Оба вон! – продолжал кричать Андрей Ефимыч. – ___!
cases.explain: «Тупые люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Go away, both!” Andrey Yefimitch went on shouting. “Stupid people! Foolish people! I don’t want either your friendship or your medicines, stupid man! Vulgar! Nasty!”

cases.sentence: Не нужно мне ни дружбы, ни твоих лекарств, ___!
cases.explain: «тупой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Go away, both!” Andrey Yefimitch went on shouting. “Stupid people! Foolish people! I don’t want either your friendship or your medicines, stupid man! Vulgar! Nasty!”

cases.sentence: Андрей Ефимыч схватил склянку с ___ и швырнул им вслед; склянка со звоном разбилась о порог.
cases.explain: «бромистым калием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Hobotov and Mihail Averyanitch, looking at each other in bewilderment, staggered to the door and went out. Andrey Yefimitch snatched up the bottle of bromide and flung it after them; the bottle broke with a crash on the doorframe.

cases.sentence: – Убирайтесь к чёрту! – крикнул он ___, выбегая в сени. – К чёрту!
cases.explain: «плачущим голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Go to the devil!” he shouted in a tearful voice, running out into the passage. “To the devil!”

cases.sentence: Извините за дружескую откровенность, – зашептал Михаил Аверьяныч, – вы живете в самой ___: теснота, нечистота, ухода за вами нет, лечиться не на что…
cases.explain: «неблагоприятной обстановке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I have never had a thought of taking offence. Illness is no joke, I understand. Your attack frightened the doctor and me yesterday, and we had a long talk about you afterwards. My dear friend, why won’t you treat your illness seriously? You can’t go on like this. … Excuse me speaking openly as a friend,” whispered Mihail Averyanitch. “You live in the most unfavourable surroundings, in a crowd, in uncleanliness, no one to look after you, no money for proper treatment. … My dear friend, the doctor and I implore you with all our hearts, listen to our advice: go into the hospital! There you will have wholesome food and attendance and treatment. Though, between ourselves, Yevgeny Fyodoritch is mauvais ton, yet he does understand his work, you can fully rely upon him. He has promised me he will look after you.”

cases.sentence: Андрей Ефимыч был тронут ___ и слезами, которые вдруг заблестели на щеках у почтмейстера.
cases.explain: «искренним участием» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Andrey Yefimitch was touched by the postmaster’s genuine sympathy and the tears which suddenly glittered on his cheeks.

cases.sentence: Болезни нет никакой, а просто я попал в ___, из которого нет выхода.
cases.explain: «заколдованный круг» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “My honoured friend, don’t believe it!” he whispered, laying his hand on his heart; “don’t believe them. It’s all a sham. My illness is only that in twenty years I have only found one intelligent man in the whole town, and he is mad. I am not ill at all, it’s simply that I have got into an enchanted circle which there is no getting out of. I don’t care; I am ready for anything.”

cases.sentence: Но, повторяю, уважаемый, я попал в ___.
cases.explain: «заколдованный круг» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Certainly I will give you my word. But I repeat, my honoured friend, I have got into an enchanted circle. Now everything, even the genuine sympathy of my friends, leads to the same thing—to my ruin. I am going to my ruin, and I have the manliness to recognize it.”

cases.sentence: – К чему это говорить? – сказал Андрей Ефимыч с раздражением. – ___ под конец жизни не испытывает того же, что я теперь.
cases.explain: «Редкий человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What’s the use of saying that?” said Andrey Yefimitch, with irritation. “There are few men who at the end of their lives do not experience what I am experiencing now. When you are told that you have something such as diseased kidneys or enlarged heart, and you begin being treated for it, or are told you are mad or a criminal—that is, in fact, when people suddenly turn their attention to you—you may be sure you have got into an enchanted circle from which you will not escape. You will try to escape and make things worse. You had better give in, for no human efforts can save you. So it seems to me.”

cases.sentence: Сдавайтесь, потому что никакие ___ уже не спасут вас.
cases.explain: «человеческие усилия» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What’s the use of saying that?” said Andrey Yefimitch, with irritation. “There are few men who at the end of their lives do not experience what I am experiencing now. When you are told that you have something such as diseased kidneys or enlarged heart, and you begin being treated for it, or are told you are mad or a criminal—that is, in fact, when people suddenly turn their attention to you—you may be sure you have got into an enchanted circle from which you will not escape. You will try to escape and make things worse. You had better give in, for no human efforts can save you. So it seems to me.”

cases.sentence: В тот же день, перед вечером, к Андрею Ефимычу неожиданно явился Хоботов в полушубке и в ___ и сказал таким тоном, как будто вчера ничего не случилось:
cases.explain: «высоких сапогах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Towards evening on the same day Hobotov, in his sheepskin and his high top-boots, suddenly made his appearance, and said to Andrey Yefimitch in a tone as though nothing had happened the day before:

cases.sentence: Думая, что Хоботов хочет развлечь его прогулкой или, в ___, дать ему заработать, Андрей Ефимыч оделся и вышел с ним на улицу.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Thinking that Hobotov wanted to distract his mind with an outing, or perhaps really to enable him to earn something, Andrey Yefimitch put on his coat and hat, and went out with him into the street. He was glad of the opportunity to smooth over his fault of the previous day and to be reconciled, and in his heart thanked Hobotov, who did not even allude to yesterday’s scene and was evidently sparing him. One would never have expected such delicacy from this uncultured man.

cases.sentence: От этого ___ трудно было ожидать такой деликатности.
cases.explain: «некультурного человека» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Thinking that Hobotov wanted to distract his mind with an outing, or perhaps really to enable him to earn something, Andrey Yefimitch put on his coat and hat, and went out with him into the street. He was glad of the opportunity to smooth over his fault of the previous day and to be reconciled, and in his heart thanked Hobotov, who did not even allude to yesterday’s scene and was evidently sparing him. One would never have expected such delicacy from this uncultured man.

cases.sentence: Вошли в больничный двор и, обойдя ___, направились к флигелю, где помещались умалишенные.
cases.explain: «главный корпус» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: They went into the hospital yard, and going round the main building, turned towards the lodge where the mental cases were kept, and all this, for some reason, in silence. When they went into the lodge Nikita as usual jumped up and stood at attention.
